newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minority party refers to intimidation.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minority party refers to intimidation.

text.p: Indonesia's minority Moslem-backed party said on Thursday it had heard reports of terror and intimidation in last week's general elections in which the ruling Golkar won a sweeping victory.
Leaders of the United Development Party (PPP) met in a Jakarta hotel to hear reports from its branches in the country's 27 provinces before deciding whether to accept the outcome of the May 29 vote.
Golkar, in power for nearly 30 years and assured of victory before a ballot was cast, swept the poll with more than 74 percent of the vote.

The PPP won just under 23 percent and the only other legal party, the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), took three percent of the poll for 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives.
PPP spokesman Usamah Hisyani told Reuters eight branches had reported to party leaders on Thursday. He said the party expected to issue a statement on its position on Friday.

"All the (eight) branches have conveyed their reports, which mostly deal with election fraud. They talk about terror and intimidation, that people should vote for a certain organisation," he said, without mentioning Golkar by name.
"They complain that on polling day PPP witnesses were not present at the polling booths," he added.
The PDI and independent monitors have also alleged irregularities in the campaign and poll, held every five years.
Attorney-General Singgih (Eds: one word), head of the official election supervisory committee, said any complaints of election rigging would be followed up.
The 27-day election campaign was the most violent in three decades, with much of the trouble between supporters of Golkar and the PPP.

Financial markets are keeping a wary eye open for the PPP decision on the election in case a rejection prompts further violence among its partisans. Money and stock markets were generally stable on Thursday, however.
Singgih told reporters after a meeting to evaluate the election that it would not be a problem if the PPP refused to sign the election results.
"According to the law, refusing to sign the results does not mean that the results are not legal. The results are still legal," he said.
He said the election commission would follow up complaints of irregularities from the PPP and PDI, adding that the poll had generally gone in an orderly fashion.
"We guarantee that we will follow up complaints about election rigging. If the violations are criminal acts...we will take further steps in accordance with the criminal law," he said.

The electoral commission held an unprecedented re-vote at Sampang on Madura island off East Java on Wednesday after angry PPP supporters rioted and burned ballot boxes following the May 29 poll on reports that Golkar had swept up the vote.
The election committee said Golkar won 57.67 percent of the vote in the strongly-Moslem Sampang Regency, including the re-vote at 65 polling stations.
The PPP got 41.93 percent and the PDI 0.38 percent. Turnout was 85 percent, it said, although witnesses said the number of voters had dropped sharply for the second poll.
